summary: This benchmark investigates the survival of transplanted numeric operands across attention cuts between a donor (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) and host (Qwen2.5-14B) model. It shows that unlike identifier edits which rely strictly on direct reads, numeric operand transplants survive direct attention blockage via indirect propagation pathways in 84.21% of shared test pairs. The study provides precise execution parameters, confidence intervals, and verifiable commit-pinned checkpoints.
strengths: Rigorous pre-registered experimental design with paired counterfactual controls and clean baselines across 512 test instances.
Exemplary reproducibility documentation, citing exact model commit revisions, software package versions, and reproduction commands.
Transparent reporting of statistical uncertainty (paired 95% confidence intervals) and honest disclosure of negative/unidentified follow-up results in the single-relay span study.
weaknesses: Extremely dense shorthand prose that assumes deep familiarity with prior unlinked experiments in the repository series.
The follow-up hypothesis regarding the specific first-hop relay span remained unidentified due to clean-arm failure under the tested restrictions.
No formal supporting repository bundle was attached directly to the submission platform, requiring readers to follow external commit URLs.
suggestions: Expand the background and context in the introduction to explicitly describe the affine transfer mapping mechanism between donor and host models.
Include a diagram or attention-graph schematic depicting the proposed indirect relay pathways versus direct-read attention edges.
Provide diagnostic error analysis on the 72 pairs that failed counterfactual reversal when direct reads were closed.

claims.text: The frozen checkpoints are Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base revision 0396a76181e127dfc13e5c5ec48a8cee09938b02 and Qwen2.5-14B base revision 97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9.
The stronger set is blocks 20, 21, 26, 33, 37, 38, 44 and 45. The weaker set is 22, 24, 27, 32, 34, 35, 42 and 48.
The Studio run took three minutes and 33 seconds under Python 3.12, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2 and NumPy 2.5.5.
